text:
mara: quick q — when a console SLO alert points to `notify.owner` (string), who actually owns the on-call? can we make ownership explicit instead of implicit team strings?

jess: +1 on making it explicit. current proto lets rules reference arbitrary tenant metadata which makes routing fuzzy. hard to trace who gets paged.

oli: the big risk is fanout. if we switch to explicit owners but keep existing fanout behavior we'll end up paging multiple teams for the same noisy signal. need a fallback chain. :warning:

samir: proposal: keep `notify.owner` but have the API return an "effective_owner" resolved list and a single "primary_owner" for paging. console shows both. API sketch: 
```json
{
  "notify_owner": "billing-team",
  "resolved_owners": ["billing-oncall", "payments-oncall"],
  "primary_owner": "billing-oncall",
  "fallback_policy": "round_robin_30m"
}
```
This lets routing layer pick one primary and still keep the chain for visibility.

liz: console UX should surface primary + why it was chosen (capacity/quota/quiet window). also show sampling rate + last routed time. users must be able to edit primary without touching the rule JSON.

mara: nice. what about quotas and sampling? if primary is overloaded we should route to fallback but also decrement quota counters. otherwise billing teams will miss signals.

oli: yep. routing must be quota-aware. suggest adding `route_score` computed from (owner_capacity, tenant_priority, quota_remaining). mutate primary only when score_delta > threshold. keep logs for telemetry.

jess: agree on telemetry. can we add a lightweight event emitted at decision time: `notify.decision` with tags: rule_id, tenant_id, chosen_owner, fallback_used, reason_code? that'll make postmortems easier.

samir: +1. also emit `notify.fanout_estimate` when a policy is evaluated for dashboards so we can predict cost.

liz: on rollouts: feature flag the resolved_owner field in the API and precompute it during ingest (not at render time) to avoid console latency. rollout plan: 1) compute in staging, 2) show read-only in console for internal teams, 3) enable edit + writeback.

mara: can someone OWN a short RFC? includes API schema, decision event spec, and console mockups. want to avoid a thousand tiny changes sneaking in.

oli: I can take the RFC. will include deterministic tie-breaker rules and quota integration.

jess: i'll draft the telemetry schema with example Prometheus labels and tracing spans.

samir: i'll add the fanout cost estimator (simple heuristic first).

liz: i'll mock the console changes. quick ask: please include a small UX affordance to "suppress fallback" so teams can opt out of being fallback for noisy tenants.

deploy-bot: scheduled: draft-rfc branch created (infra/rfc/notify-ownership-1765433333) — run tests when ready. :robot_face:

mara: awesome. timeline: RFC by EOW, staging rollout next sprint. thanks all!

jess: tiny nit — pls include migration path for existing rules that reference freeform tags. recommend a one-time mapping UI that suggests resolved owners based on tenant metadata.

oli: noted. will add migration section.

samir: tagging: @liz for UX, @jess for telemetry, @mara for product signoff.

liz: got it, will start mocks tomorrow.

mara: closing loop: I'll post an RFC template link and a quick acceptance checklist in #eng-platform.

mara: (also: can we add an audit log line when anyone edits the primary_owner via console?)

oli: yes — audit required. add `audit.edit_primary_owner` event.

mara: perfect.
